cues.text: TriedPath Fellowship presents:
Understanding Your Roots.
Part one. How your mind works.
Our mind works like a computer.

It is constantly placing information into
categories.

If you feed something destructive into
your mind,

it will add this to a stack of similar
material already there.

As the stack grows larger, it gains in
power.
In the computer industry, the saying is:
garbage in, garbage out.

It is our responsibility to see that the
new information

we receive is consistent with our new
life.
New from TriedPath: Mountains of Material!
Scripture memory, on twelve cassettes.

In the car. In the kitchen. At your
bedside.
Fill your memory tapes,
and push the old material out!
Operators are standing by!
End of part one. Question two.

Have you ever been able to stop thinking
about something?
Did you succeed?
Pause the tape, and write your answer.
Part two. Your roots.
You were not born this way.
It grew, one response at a time.
And what was learned can be unlearned.
A child's security rests on three bonds:
mother to child, father to child,
and father to mother.

Any break in this triangle produces
insecurity.
Real, or only perceived,
the results are the same.

Between two and six, a boy must leave his
mother's world,

and his father must welcome him into his
own.
But a boy with no welcome from his father
finds none among the boys.

So he stays in the kitchen, with his
mother.
He compares himself with other boys.
Comparison becomes admiration.
Admiration slips into envy.
At puberty, the envy becomes eroticized.
Part three. Displacement.
Putting off, putting on.

Displacement is the idea that one thing
pushes out another.
There is no neutral ground.

If there is a vacancy there, evil will
fill it.

Interference is the technical name for
displacement.

New material coming into your mind pushes
the old material out.
In thirty days, we forget eighty percent
of what we learned.
For you, that is a blessing.

Turn on any radio or television, and you
will find

a mind-boggling barrage of new morality
propaganda.

Gays on television are shown as superior
people.
What do we lose?

The associations, triggered by music,
clothing,
and many other things.
Bars will close. The scene will change.
Question five.

What do you do when associations from the
past overwhelm you?
Pause the tape, and write your answer.

So fill your memory tapes with new
material,
until the bulk of it ejects the old.

We forget things that are contrary to our
opinions.
If we are ambivalent, the new information
will find no permanent home in our minds.
This places the burden directly on us.
For further study:
booklet one, from our Pocket Library.
Homosexual people say they never asked
for their orientation.
In most cases, that is true.
Something they never chose.

thoughts, the more intense they become.”

music, their friends, their places.

a journal, and report each week.

failure was theirs.

It was written for pastors, counselors and
lay workers.

cues.text: [upbeat music]
Is a friendship getting too close?
The little booklet with the checklist.
Order a five-pack for your group.

Grab your journal and your workbook,
friend.
Today we go underneath.
Every tree is known by its fruit.

But fruit grows from roots, and roots grow
in soil.

For women, the classic teaching names
three things in the soil:

our relationships, our identity, and how
we picture God.
It's not a sexual orientation problem.
It's an identity crisis.
Let's pause the DVD here, friend.

Turn to page thirty-one, and talk it
through with your group.

A little girl first learns who she is from
her mother.

If Mom seems distant, critical or
overbearing,
she may pull back to protect herself.

The teaching calls it defensive
detachment.
A girl looks to her mother for the model,
and to her father for the grade.
His words become her score card:
passing or failing as a little girl.
[upbeat music]
Twenty Monday evenings.

A hundred and fifty dollars covers your
materials.
Ask about payment plans.
Groups fill up in days!

Here's a picture from an older teaching —
1993.
Remember floppy disks?

To use a computer analogy, a heterosexual
woman
has a floppy disc that is titled “woman,”

so each experience that is related to her
femaleness
can be stored in that file.

The lesbian woman receives information
relating to femininity,
but she has no file to put it in.
The “information” and experiences
that should affirm her get lost.
Save that one, friend.

Emotional dependency is when someone
else's presence
feels necessary for your security.

When anyone takes the centre that belongs
to God,
the old booklet calls it idolatry.
Here are the signs.
Whether or not anything physical happens,
sin has entered the friendship.

Now, many of these things aren't sinful in
themselves.

Romantic gestures and certain kinds of
exclusivity

are completely appropriate in marriage and
engagement.

…and sometimes even in a serious dating
relationship.
[music stops]

TALK IT THROUGH · 10 minutes
1. Look at the tree on page 22. What is in your soil?
2. Which of the Big Three do you recognise in your own story?
3. Pray for one another before you press play.

“Prepare for grief
and depression.”

“…as painful as
going through
a divorce.”

It asked women to
end their closest
friendships.

To throw away
the songs they
shared.

To confess their
feelings, and be
asked about them
again and again.

To look for
the cause in their
mothers and fathers.

When the feelings
stayed, it said
they had not truly
wanted to change.

In June 2016 it
was still sold
in packs of five.

cues.text:
HEDGE™. A course for parents, in a
confused age.

I thought I'd know. I thought I'd see it
coming.

Your child is not confused. Your child is
being confused.

We saw it coming. For almost forty years,
we have watched it grow.
Lesson one. 1988. The Old Wound.
We were answering these calls in 1988.

We called it a false identity. Find the
hurt, and you find the root.
And we still call it a false identity.
Usually, the hurt was in the family.
Was it us?

The same roots as homosexuality. Only
deeper.
Your homework: find the root.

Someone has a plan for your child. Have
yours. Free. Live. Tonight.

Module one, complete. Module two unlocks
when you're ready.
Lesson two. 2003. Catch It Early.

Are you afraid your child may be
struggling with gender identity?

We told the churches: a young girl in
Sunday school that might have some gender
identity deficits can be helped.
Prevention tops the list.
Your homework: watch for the early signs.
Lesson three. 2014. The Culture Moved In.

Then it wasn't one family any more. It
came through public education, popular
culture and social media.

If your children have unmonitored access
to the internet, you are a negligent
parent.

Your homework: know how many times she
texts.

Add her name. Every member prays for her,
at least once a day.
Lesson four. 2016. It Spreads.

It arrived decades ago as a tiny seed. Now
it's in our homes.

One friend comes out. Then the group. Then
your daughter.

Your homework: share this lesson with five
families.
Lesson five. 2025. It Has a Name.
A culture swept up by gender ideology.
Now even governments use our word.
The numbers speak for themselves.

Your homework: pray for her protection
from the negative influence of others.
Lesson six. Today. When She Is 18.

Those under 18 can involve a full-court
press approach,

while young adults will have the liberty
to make their own choices.
The liberty to make their own choices.
She's eighteen now.

So love her over the long term. It can
take seven to ten years.

Ask anything, any hour. And when you're
ready, a real person. Free.

If you care about your daughter, finish
the course.

In their own words, 2019:
“No one is certain what
causes gender confusion.”
Then they listed causes.

First the family.
Then her friends.
Then the whole culture.

Nothing was dropped.
Each reason was added
to the ones before.

Parents were told
to find the wound,
to watch for signs,
to monitor her phone.

Parenthood was made
a political identity;
the child, a figure to
build coalitions around.

At 18, their own post says,
she is free to choose.

Her parents were told:
it can take
seven to ten years.

The WHO: trans-related
identities are not
conditions of
mental ill-health.
